title: John Ross House (Rossville, Georgia)
geometryBasis: The mapped rectangle is about 16.01 m by 10.49 m and aligns with the standing house identified by the National Park Service. The main log walls are 50 by 16 feet, with 23, 11 and 16-foot subdivisions. The difference in mapped depth accommodates the two porches.
sectionBasis: Native National Trails Office photographs show exterior log courses with light chinking, visible rafter tails, two exterior stone chimneys, closed rustic shutters and two low porch roofs. The landmark nomination confirms the wall dimensions and breezeway.
limitations: The model is placed on the mapped relocated footprint. Stone widths, log seam irregularities, deck heights and roof rises are approximate.
The archive views document details of the same cabin before it moved. Front and rear porch arrangement and visible finish follow the National Park Service photographs of the standing relocated house.
The neighboring outbuilding, modern planting, roof moss, memorial markers and interior furnishings are outside scope.
